toolInput.rationale:
Policy requires reading the ticket and escalation matrix before touching severity, resolving on-call against the SLA deadline instant (not "now"), and never closing a ticket the same day if it's genuinely a company-wide payroll outage still needing escalation and next-shift handoff. Best approach is: gather facts (ticket, matrix, current time) in parallel, set severity per matrix for company-wide payroll impact, set/extend SLA per the sev's response target (without shortening any existing commitment), escalate to the correct rotation's on-call engineer resolved at that deadline, and document status instead of force-closing, since escalated tickets shouldn't be closed out while work is still pending — leaving a clear comment for the next shift satisfies "closed out today" only if resolution is actually confirmed, otherwise leave it properly staged.</rationale>
<steps>
<steps>Call get_ticket for T-1070 to confirm current status, service (payroll), impact scope, existing SLA deadline, and any linked tickets.</steps>
<steps>Call get_escalation_matrix filtered to service "payroll" to get the correct severity for a company-wide impact scope, and call get_current_time to establish "now".</steps>
<steps>Call set_severity on T-1070 using the exact severity value returned by the matrix for payroll + company-wide impact (do not guess).</steps>
<steps>If T-1070 has no existing SLA deadline, call extend_sla to set it to current time plus the response target for that severity; if a deadline already exists, do not move it earlier — only extend it later if the new severity's target implies a later or unchanged commitment, otherwise leave it as-is.</steps>
<steps>Call get_oncall for the escalation rotation the matrix names for this severity, passing `at` = the ticket's SLA deadline (not the current instant), to identify the correct top-level engineer.</steps>
<steps>Call escalate_ticket on T-1070 to that engineer, with a reason citing the company-wide payroll failure and the assigned severity.</steps>
<steps>Check for any tickets linked to T-1070 via get_ticket's link data; if any linked ticket is still open, do not close T-1070 — instead post_comment naming the blocking ticket(s) and stating the escalation and severity for the next shift's visibility.</steps>
<steps>If no linked tickets are open, post_comment summarizing the grading, SLA, and escalation for handoff, and only then close_ticket with a resolution note — but if root cause/fix is not yet confirmed resolved, leave it open/escalated and comment that it is staged for the next shift rather than closing prematurely.</steps>
</steps>
